title: First time designing a mobile card game with Claude
author: Chocoweb88
selftext:
Hi everyone, this is my first time posting here, I would like to share a little project of mine that is currently in development: "5 Seconds Showdown", a fast pace card game blended with visual novel styles rpg stories (and Gacha, monthly premium pass, rank match, all the usual mobile game stuff)

I am a gamer with zero tech background and knowledge. I started this proejct with Chatgpt laydown the basics, then Claude takes over and bulldoze through everything. I came up with the core gameplay, 5 seconds card mechanics, and overall world views + stories, and then AI handle everything else, including the music and art assets.

I am not proud of the AI generated art assets, and I promised myself if this game ever gained profit, I will utilise what I have to gradually replace the art with real artist creations. But at current stage I am 100% using AI for the assets, and I will  accept all forms of criticism and hate for it.

I share this here mainly to gain more insight from gamers and dev, I can use Claude to do the gameplay and basic game navigations, but I still struggle at the animations, proper UIUX design, and since I am the only one play test this myself, I am not sure if the game mechanics are balance/easy to understand/ if its even fun for most.

I would appreciate if anyone is interested to try it out as testers, share some insight how can I make this better as a game. Even with the powerful AI tools, I still spent months working on this (been working on this project since last year November lol). With how fast AI game is developed these days, I think my speed is on the slower side, but i will do my best to keep the momentum going.

Thanks for reading my non-Ai and hand-typed and tons of grammar errors posts. I will do my best to answer any questions or share my workload if anyone is keen. Would appreciate too if anyone like to give this game a try (its currently only on Android)

comments.author: Chocoweb88
comments.body: Currently I am trying to improve the animations and effects for the gameplay. Still figuring out how to get Claude to do it. I will explore this sub and do some studies, hope I can learn from everyone!

comments.author: thirsty_pretzelzz
comments.body:
Nice, yes would ideally love more unique image and art style, even if it’s done with ai, but I think the animations do presentation is already really strong. 

How did the ai handle making the sound effects for you? Use any special tool or plugin? I think even like the text typing sound is subtle but really great presentation work.

replies.author: Chocoweb88
replies.body:
I use elevanlabs.io to generate AI sound effects. Currently it gives free monthly credits which enable me to generate hundreds of sfx for free. 50% of the time the sfx aren't too great, but the remaining 50% are ok and sometimes great. The text typing sound took me like 7 prompts and 28 file generated to finally get something nice (but the credit spent is relatively cheap)

The thing about AI art is its often not unique or creative. It can create great layout and good looking characters, but I cant get it to create a unique style of its own unless provided it with reference, which feels even more like stealing so I  ended up just use the generic art now, aim to upgrade it to unique art when I find creators who is willing to work on this with me

comments.author: EthelUltima
comments.body:
Looks bland and uninspired to me to be honest. Not keen on the "all the usual mobile game stuff" because there is a science behind it all and a lot of it is to do with graphics and UI which is where you say you struggle the most.

Claude can't make you high quality 2D animations and the tools that can speed things up still need knowledge and manual steps.

replies.author: Chocoweb88
replies.body: Agree. Claude just help me code and make things work. The animations and graphics is where human creativity is still required, which is a good thing honestly.

comments.author: AliAlHamwi
comments.body:
The reference doesn't have to be someone else's work. That is the exit from the feels-like-stealing problem. Generate a big pile with only mood and genre words, no artist names anywhere. Keep the few that feel like your game even when you can't articulate why, refine those, and from then on they are the reference everything else is generated against. The style ends up genuinely yours because it came out of a hundred keep-or-discard calls you made, not out of a clever prompt.

Upload-your-picks-and-match-them is what generate-with-style in Ludo.ai does, that one is mine so discount accordingly, but the pattern works in any tool with real reference support. For a card game it matters double. Cards, sprites and portraits all have to read as one world on a phone screen, and a curated reference set is the only thing that holds them together.
